properties.title: Generating Counterfactual Patient Timelines from Real-World Data

membership.reason: Autoregressive GPT-2 transformer simulating multi-day longitudinal EHR patient timelines with Monte Carlo rollouts under baseline covariate perturbations.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L1 predictive EHR trajectory world model (WT_EHR, BP_FORECAST); lacks action-conditioned intervention modeling.

properties.backbone: 12-block GPT-2 decoder-only transformer (d_model=768, 12 heads, d_seq=2048) with categorical/numeric/temporal/admission encodings

properties.flow: HL7 EHR timeline prompt (with perturbed age/CRP/creatinine) -> 12-layer GPT-2 autoregressive Monte Carlo rollout (S=256, 7 days) -> event rates

properties.purpose: 7-day hospital outcome and treatment-pattern simulation under baseline lab/demographic perturbations.
properties.environment: Single-center retrospective University of Tokyo Hospital EHR (2011-2023)

assertions.rationale: Minute-level chronological timeline ordering with discretized time-progression tokens.
HL7 v2.5 records mapped to ICD-10 diagnoses, ATC medications, JLAC10 labs, and 2,000 percentile numeric bins.
Separate categorical, numeric (2-layer GeLU), temporal (5D age), and admission-status encodings.
Autoregressive transformer hidden state over sequential clinical timeline.
Conditioned on full chronological patient prompt timeline.
Autoregressive next-entry generation over 7-day hospital horizon.
12-layer GPT-2 decoder-only transformer trained with cross-entropy.
Monte Carlo sampling (S=256 rollouts per admission) from softmax next-entry distribution.

Next-entry future timeline prediction is scored on 7,496 held-out validation patients (validation cross-entropy loss 2.640 vs training 2.564, p. 6), and 7-day autoregressive Monte Carlo rollouts (S=256) on 2023 COVID-19 admissions compare perturbed simulated event rates (R_s) against observed real 2023 rates (R_r) and clinical reference directions (Fig. 2, Table 2; CRP and creatinine shifts match expected patterns, age shifts are mixed for remdesivir/LOS). Limitation: unperturbed 7-day predictive accuracy/calibration on the 7% holdout test set is not reported.
Patient-level counterfactual risk and clinical-trajectory simulation.
Approved by University of Tokyo Research Ethics Committee (2023367NI).
Clinical plausibility of 7-day simulated mortality, LOS>7d, and remdesivir rates under age/CRP/creatinine perturbations (Fig. 2).
Simulations complete in <1 second on GPU with KV caching.

evidence_fragments.content: Here, we show that an autoregressive generative model, trained on real-world data from over 300,000 patients and 400 million patient timeline entries, can generate clinically plausible counterfactual trajectories. As a validation task, we applied the model to patients hospitalized with COVID-19 in 2023, modifying age, serum C-reactive protein (CRP), and serum creatinine to simulate 7-day outcomes.

[paraphrase (visual p.3)] Figure 1a-b shows structured clinical records converted into chronologically ordered patient timelines with categorical embeddings, numeric encoder, temporal encoder, and admission status encodings passed through 12 decoder-only transformer blocks and a prediction head/softmax to autoregressively sample next entries.

[paraphrase (visual p.7)] Figure 2 shows 7-day Monte Carlo (S=256) simulation responses to prompt perturbations of age (n=195), serum CRP (n=184), and serum creatinine (n=183) vs actual 2023 rates: higher in-hospital mortality with older age (age+15y plotted as p=0.0555 in Fig. 2a vs text p=0.0055), higher CRP (up to p=0.0031), and higher creatinine (p<0.0001); increased remdesivir use with higher CRP (p=0.0095) and decreased remdesivir use with higher creatinine (p=0.0002).

While evaluating alternative treatment strategies—such as medication choices—is a critical objective for counterfactual simulation in clinical medicine, we did not explore such interventions in this study due to unresolved methodological challenges.
The final training and validation loss was 2.564 and 2.640, respectively.
This study was reviewed and approved by the Research Ethics Committee of the University of Tokyo (Approval Number: 2023367NI).

Encoded vectors were interleaved in chronological order to construct the input matrix, which was passed through a stack of 12 decoder-only transformer blocks. Each block followed the GPT-2 architecture11, including its weight initialization scheme.
We included patients from the training dataset for the simulation assessment due to the small number of events, which limited statistical power.

capability_assessments.rationale: Unconditioned 12-layer GPT-2 autoregressive EHR timeline generator with held-out validation next-entry loss (2.640 on 7,496 patients) and 7-day Monte Carlo rollouts (S=256) evaluated for directional agreement against observed 2023 rates under baseline prompt perturbations (age/CRP/creatinine); explicitly does not model treatment interventions and does not report unperturbed holdout test discrimination/calibration (L1).

limitations: Does not model treatment/medication interventions; only independent baseline covariate perturbations.
Single-center retrospective data with patient overlap between 2011-2022 training and 2023 simulation cohorts.

Unperturbed future-outcome discrimination/calibration metrics on the reserved 7% holdout test set are not reported (only validation cross-entropy loss 2.640 and perturbed 7-day directional comparisons against observed 2023 rates). Visual inspection of Fig. 2a (p. 7) also noted a p-value printing discrepancy for age+15y mortality (p=0.0555 in plot vs p=0.0055 in text).
notes: All 10 physical PDF pages extracted/read; pages 3 and 7 visually inspected via rendered PNGs.

legacy_cells.B: Generating Counterfactual Patient Timelines from Real-World Data
legacy_cells.C: Akagi, Yu, Seki, Tomohisa, Takiguchi, Toru, Ito, Hiromasa, Kawazoe, Yoshimasa, Ohe, Kazuhiko
legacy_cells.S: How do altered age, CRP, or creatinine values in hospitalized COVID-19 patients affect generated 7-day clinical timelines and event probabilities?
legacy_cells.T: COVID-19 admissions in 2023 with SARS-CoV-2 confirmed by positive PCR or antigen test within 24 hours before or after admission; CRP and creatinine experiments additionally required a recorded relevant measurement.
legacy_cells.X: F2 EHR / ICU event & latent patient dynamics
legacy_cells.AI: Structured EHR: age and sex; diagnoses; medication prescriptions; laboratory test codes and results; admission/discharge events; time-progression entries
legacy_cells.AJ: Categorical entries use embedding layers; numeric values use a two-feed-forward-layer GeLU encoder; age uses a temporal encoder of the same architecture; encoded entries pass through 12 GPT-2-style decoder-only transformer blocks.
legacy_cells.BL: Time progression is discretized into 10-minute bins for intervals under 24 hours; longer intervals use coarser day-interval bins and 1-hour time-of-day subdivisions.
legacy_cells.BS: Autoregressively generated future patient-timeline entries, including diagnoses, medications, laboratory results, time progression, and discharge/outcome events.
legacy_cells.BT: Next-entry probability distribution over the timeline vocabulary.
legacy_cells.DN: Longitudinal electronic health records from the University of Tokyo Hospital
legacy_cells.DQ: 373,890 unique patients in the overall dataset; counterfactual cohorts: 195 age-simulation admissions, 184 CRP-simulation admissions, and 183 creatinine-simulation admissions.
legacy_cells.EA: Outcome trends were compared with expected clinical patterns: increased age/CRP/creatinine generally increased simulated mortality; higher creatinine reduced simulated remdesivir use; higher CRP increased remdesivir use.
legacy_cells.ED: Compared simulated scenario event rates with actual-data rates and expected directions; direct counterfactual outcome validation was unavailable because the counterfactual outcomes cannot be observed.
legacy_cells.EG: Training: 2 days 5 hours on four NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs. 622,592 counterfactual simulations completed in 9 hours 3 minutes; reported average runtime 0.052 seconds per simulation.
legacy_cells.EL: Age-modified simulations showed no consistent trend in remdesivir use or prolonged hospitalization; creatinine-modified prolonged-stay trends were not statistically significant.
legacy_cells.ER: Research Ethics Committee of the University of Tokyo, approval number 2023367NI.
legacy_cells.FL: Structured clinical EHR entries are encoded by categorical, numeric, or temporal pathways, interleaved chronologically, and processed by a 12-block decoder-only transformer; a prediction head generates the next-entry distribution, with autoregressive sampling producing timelines. No planner is described.
legacy_cells.FM: The authors adapt a decoder-only autoregressive transformer for patient timelines and demonstrate scenario simulations after modifying patient age, CRP, and creatinine in COVID-19 admissions.
legacy_cells.FN: In 195 age-simulation admissions, mortality increased most at age +15 years (p = 0.0055). In CRP simulations, mortality and remdesivir-use trends increased with CRP; prolonged stay was significantly elevated at +150 and +200 mg/L (p = 0.0270 and 0.0070). In creatinine simulations, remdesivir use declined and mortality increased; 622,592 total simulations ran at 0.052 seconds per simulation on average.
legacy_cells.FO: Modifications covered only a small set of variables and were applied independently; analysis focused exclusively on COVID-19 admissions; treatment-strategy interventions were not explored because of unresolved causal-simulation challenges; few events limited statistical power; further validation across diverse scenarios and evaluation frameworks is needed.
legacy_cells.FP: The authors call for testing across more diverse clinical scenarios and development of evaluation frameworks for counterfactual predictions.
legacy_cells.FQ: Prior generative models had demonstrated realistic patient timelines, but their use for patient-level counterfactual simulation had remained unexplored.
legacy_cells.FR: The experiments demonstrate scenario sensitivity to modified age and laboratory values, not identified treatment-effect counterfactuals: treatment choices were not intervened on, causal identification assumptions/methods were not reported, and counterfactual ground-truth outcomes were unavailable. Results are retrospective and from one hospital; they do not establish prospective clinical benefit or decision usefulness.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M6 Rollout service; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Expose future-state forecasts through a time-aware dynamics interface and validate error versus horizon; treatment actions need separate evidence before intervention simulation.
legacy_cells.FX: Title/abstract and Introduction; Methods (ethics, data acquisition, model formulation and architecture, Table 1, pretraining, COVID-19 cohort and simulation design, Table 2); Results (dataset, pretraining, age/CRP/creatinine results and Figure 2); Discussion and limitations; Conclusion.
